crops_forage_v2:
Use case: style-transfer. Asset type: a single production sprite sheet, a unified family of crop and forage sprites for the existing Pixel Farm Godot game. The attached first image is the EXACT style reference: existing original crop_growth_v1.png. The second image is the EXACT small inventory-icon reference. Replace the subjects with the new subjects below, retaining the reference's simple shapes, broad solid color clusters, soft pastel yellow-green leaves, muted mauve-brown one-pixel outlines, cream highlights and very limited shading. The current new blueberry sprites are rejected for being too intricate and realistically woody. This sheet must look as if drawn by the artist who drew the reference carrot and turnip. Do NOT copy from Stardew Valley or any outside game.
Output one transparent square 4-column by 4-row regular sprite sheet, 16 sprites total, equally spaced cells with large transparent gutters; no labels, no text, no grid lines, no background, no checkerboard baked into pixels. Each sprite is a genuine coarse pixel drawing on a 32x32 logical cell, enlarged with nearest-neighbor block pixels. Strictly square visible pixels, no painterly texture, no anti-aliasing, no gradients, no glow, no dithering, no fine leaf veins or thin tangled stems. Approx 6-9 flat colors per sprite. Outline weight and simplicity identical to reference. Orthographic front/top-down farm-game view. Plants have a small muted brown soil mound and base on same bottom baseline. Early plants remain small; never normalize sprout size to mature size.
Exact cell content, left to right, top to bottom:
ROW 1: blueberry sprout (two rounded light green leaves, 8 logical pixels tall); blueberry young plant (four broad rounded leaves, 13px tall); blueberry growing plant (simple rounded light green leafy bush, a few small green berries, 18px tall); ripe blueberry bush (same simple green silhouette, just three to five large distinct powder-blue/lavender berries, 23px tall, max 22px wide, NO woody bramble).
ROW 2: potato sprout (two leaves, 8px tall); potato young plant (four rounded leaves, 13px tall); potato growing plant (simple leaves, 18px tall); ripe potato plant (simple rounded leaves, two cream blossoms and two golden potatoes at soil base, 23px tall).
ROW 3: harvested blueberries icon (three plump powder-blue berries and one light green leaf); wild blackberries icon (two softly muted violet berries with simple large round lobes and one leaf, NOT a black thorny cluster); wild mushroom icon (one squat cream mushroom with pastel warm tan cap); wild flower icon (one cream flower with golden center and two light green leaves).
ROW 4: blueberry seed packet icon (small cream paper seed pouch with blue berry symbol, no text); potato seed packet icon (same pouch design with golden potato symbol); harvested potato icon (one simple golden potato); pickled tomato jar icon (small glass jar, cream lid, soft salmon-red tomato inside).
For rows 3-4 icons, use maximum 22x22 logical pixels centered within their cells. Use just 2 shades per material and a cream single-pixel highlight. Keep outlines quiet, green leaves bright soft pastel matching the original reference. Transparent alpha outside each sprite. Exact regular grid, all sixteen subjects entirely separated.
wild_berries_v2:
Use case: style-transfer. Asset type: ONE cohesive 4x4 sprite sheet for a three-species wild berry grove in a Godot pixel-farm game.
Reference image 1 basic_grass_biom_things.png is the exact game-world art direction. In particular inspect the small mint/sage green berry bushes near the lower left: rounded, broad simple shapes, dusty sage outlines, pastel mint-green highlights. Reference image 2 crop_growth_v1.png shows the game's crop silhouette simplicity and pixel scale. Match these references closely. Replace the current mismatching dark-green procedural circle bushes with original low-resolution pixel sprites. No copying from any outside game.
Output: transparent 1024x1024 square, exact 4 columns x 4 rows of equal cells; isolated sprites centered horizontally and aligned to a common ground baseline per cell; generous transparent gutters, no text, no labels, no grid lines, no baked checkerboard, no landscape. Each world sprite has a 32x32 logical pixel canvas, rendered as crisp nearest-neighbor enlarged square pixels; visible mature bush 22-26 logical pixels wide and 15-18 logical pixels tall. Only 5-8 large flat color clusters per sprite, 1px outline in muted sage/taupe (never black), two tones for foliage, warm cream highlights. No blur, soft gradients, texture noise, tiny realistic leaves, visible veins, woody thickets, vector circles or smooth edges.
Exact cell order:
ROW 1: blackberry seedling (small mint-green two-leaf sprout, 8px tall); blackberry mature bare bush (rounded mint and sage foliage only, broad simple 3-lobed silhouette); same blackberry mature bush with four large clearly visible muted lavender-purple ripe berries; harvested blackberry icon (two purple softly lobed berries and a mint leaf, tiny simple icon).
ROW 2: raspberry seedling; raspberry mature bare bush; same bush with four large dusty coral-pink ripe raspberries; harvested raspberry icon (two dusty coral-pink berries with green cap).
ROW 3: gooseberry seedling; gooseberry mature bare bush; same bush with four soft pastel yellow-green round gooseberries; harvested gooseberry icon (two yellow-green berries and leaf).
ROW 4: blackberry seed packet (cream paper pouch with purple berry symbol, NO text); raspberry seed packet (matching pouch with pink berry symbol); gooseberry seed packet (matching pouch with yellow-green berry symbol); a small neutral three-leaf mint sprout.
The 3 foliage forms may have slight silhouette differences to distinguish species but MUST share palette, outline weight, scale and camera. Ripe and bare pairs have identical size, base and leaf silhouette so picking fruit visually removes only the berries. Seedlings are visibly much smaller than adults. Ground base a tiny soft tan tuft like reference bushes, no big dirt disks or pots. Inventory icons and seed packets max20x20 logical pixels, centered in cell. Transparent alpha outside sprites. This must be as simple, soft and bright as the actual game's existing mint-green bushes.
